effect_estimate.comment: No primary statistical analysis or quantitative effect estimate is produced; figures mentioned (e.g., 18% construction cost reduction in IRC 1988; up to 70% non-functioning systems in Black 1989) are cited descriptively from secondary reports. Extracted strictly from provided PDF (Rondinelli 1991), which does not match the Asthana (2003) header citation.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Narrative synthesis of secondary project evaluations concludes that centralized government ministries struggle to extend and maintain rural and peri-urban water systems due to institutional fragmentation and weak O&M, whereas decentralized community management succeeds when six mutually reinforcing factors are present: (1) adequate user and bureaucratic incentives (including legal transfer of system ownership to communities and labour-for-connection/fee arrangements), (2) training and organizational skills/resources, (3) institutionalized procedures for community consultation, O&M contracting, and ownership turnover, (4) cooperative interorganizational relationships across communities, NGOs, and government agencies, (5) locally repairable VLOM technology and spare-parts supply, and (6) continuous monitoring, evaluation, and feedback systems.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Summary; Table 1, PDF pp. 6-7; PDF pp. 2-15
